question: During a meeting of the Council Working Party on Tax Questions (WPTQ) on 30 March 2023, representatives of the Member States discussed the automatic exchange of tax information with third countries and its interaction with the General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR).

The Presidency steering note shows that Member States analysed whether this automatic exchange of tax information with third countries respects appropriate data protection safeguards, seeking to identify the gaps and to reach a common understanding among Member States on an appropriate level of safeguards.1 Against this background, 1.

Did the Commission attend this and/or other meeting(s) in this context? If so, what is the result of the WPTQ’s work on mapping and agreeing on safeguards for the automatic exchange of tax information with third countries?
Does the Commission consider that Article 49 of the GDPR applies to the automatic exchange of tax information with third countries insofar as it concerns mass data transfer?

If not, and if the automatic exchange of tax information with third countries is based on Article 46 of the GDPR, does the Commission consider that in the absence of guarantees stated in a legally binding document, the automatic exchange of tax information with third countries is compliant with the GDPR?
Presidency Steering note, WPTQ meeting, 30 March 2023
answer: Agreements between Member States and third countries on the automatic exchange of tax information are aimed at eliminating opportunities for non-taxation or reduced taxation through fraud, tax evasion or tax avoidance; and are therefore an important general public interest of Member States.

At the same time, this important general public interest needs to be pursued in compliance with the individuals’ fundamental right to the protection of their personal data. Therefore, work is ongoing in the Council of the EU to enhance legal certainty concerning the application of data protection requirements in the context of these agreements.

The Commission’s services, including through their participation in the meetings of the Council Working Party on Tax Questions, are supporting this work in close cooperation with the relevant Presidency.
Presidency Steering note, WPTQ meeting, 30 March 2023
